Project VektaKillzone HD: Unofficial PC Port (static recompilation)

A native Linux and Windows x64 port of the 2011 PS3 remaster of the first Killzone, made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and compiled into a PC program on your machine; graphics go through Vulkan. No emulator runs at play time.

Status: Partly playable

You need your own copy of the game. This project ships no game code, data, assets or keys.

See the statusSource on GitHub

Screens

Screenshots of the port running the developer's own copy of the game, kept to document progress; the game content in them belongs to Sony Interactive Entertainment and Guerrilla Games. Every screenshot, by date: SCREENSHOTS.md.

Unreleased

not released yet

  • AddedDeveloper tools for performance work (docs/dev/perf-bench.md, docs/dev/performance.md): KZ_ROUTE_REBASE writes a route replay out as a route of the current build, so that later replays follow it exactly; tools/perf/ab.sh compares two builds in alternating runs on a route and reports the paired difference; ps3recomp patch 3034 (a guest store journal, built only with -DKZ_STORE_JOURNAL=ON) lets KZ_NATIVE_VERIFY check native functions with wide effects against their lifted bodies. Off unless used; the game itself is unchanged.
  • ChangedLess CPU for the same frames: the draw engine keeps the converted vertices of draws the game repeats unchanged (about 70 % of them) in GPU memory instead of converting them again every frame. On the Level 7 and Level 1 test routes the RSX thread uses 0.5-0.6 ms less per frame (about 13-15 %), the whole game about 4-7 % less; frame rates the same. PS3RECOMP_ENG_VCACHE=0 turns it off (after ps3recomp pull request #718).
  • Changedtools/pgo.sh (optional profile-guided build): it makes its own play folder (work/vfs-test) from work/vfs instead of failing on a fresh clone, ends with a check that the profile matches the lifted code (a stale profile was silently ignored), shows a failing step's log instead of hiding it, and can train on recorded routes (KZ_PGO_ROUTES). An instrumented build now writes its profile when the game quits, so a route replay that ends on its own leaves one. Measured gain on ps3recomp v0.19.0: about +2 % average fps with the default play, about +4 % trained on combat routes (docs/BUILDING.md).
  • ChangedLess CPU while the game waits for its next frame: at the default 60 fps the main thread spun through the wait and stayed about 99 % busy; it now sleeps until shortly before the next tick of the game clock and takes the tick exactly as before, about half a core less (KZ_FRAME_WAIT_SPIN=1 goes back to spinning). The SPURS scheduler now runs only the work the game asked for, without probing idle SPUs, which used 4.6 to 6 % less CPU for the whole game on the Level 7 and Level 1 test routes with the same frame rates (PS3_SPURS_WANTED=0 goes back to the old way; after Project Helghast's patch 1074) (docs/dev/performance.md).
  • FixedReservations: after many thread starts a thread could stop being told when another one broke its reservation (ps3recomp patch 3037, after upstream pull request #758).
  • FixedScripted events at 60 and 144 fps: the level scripts' update ran once per frame, so above 30 fps everything they count in updates ran 2 to 5 times too fast. In the last level the platform ride to the main station took about 12 s instead of about 49 s, the story events timed in seconds fell behind it and the section never ended. The update now runs 30 times per second of game time, as on the PS3, at every frame rate, and also on any frame with script messages waiting (area triggers, finished dialogue), which the game drops after the update (KZ_SCRIPT_EVERY_FRAME=1 goes back to the old way). Objects a script moves step by step, such as that platform, slide a little every frame instead of jumping 30 times a second, which also made the voices of the characters riding it sound robotic (KZ_SCRIPT_SMOOTH=0 turns the sliding off).
  • FixedVulkan: a start without DLSS or FSR 3.1 after one with them no longer builds the upscaler's pipelines ahead, which the Vulkan validation layer reported as an error (VUID-VkPipelineColorBlendStateCreateInfo-pAttachments-00605); independentBlend is now on whenever the GPU has it (patch 2061).

0.4.0

9 Nov 2026 · pre-release

  • AddedDeveloper switches for testing (docs/dev/testing.md): KZ_DEBUG_GOD=1 keeps the game's own God mode on, KZ_DEBUG_GIVE gives the player weapons and grenades once per level through the game's own PLAYER:AddWeapon, and KZ_PROF=key,<seconds>,<file> records a CPU profile each time F11 is pressed in the game's window. All are off unless set.
  • ChangedField of view: the PC page's Field of View row is now the horizontal FOV at 16:9, 70 to 120 degrees (the game's is 87), with a second row, Weapon Field of View, for the first-person weapon; a wider window still shows more at the sides. A setting from an older version (vertical) is carried over.
  • Changedps3recomp moved from v0.18.0 to v0.19.0: its SPURS, GCM, lv2 and file system fixes (81 pull requests). The patch series was re-applied: 1006 dropped (now upstream), 1017 smaller, 0006 to 0008 new; the Vulkan backend stays the port's. Levels 1 to 8 replay to their end; speed the same or better (levels 3, 4 and 8 faster) (docs/dev/ps3recomp-v019-migration.md).
  • FixedInstalling over an earlier version no longer fails at the link with undefined symbols (seen from the 0.3.1 test build to 0.4.0's: ppu_thread_register_main_priority, ppu_thread_set_main_stack, issue #18). The setup program and the release archives give every source file one fixed date, older than the objects the earlier build left, so Ninja took those objects as up to date and kept the earlier version's code; removing only CMake's cache did not change that. A build folder made from another version or patch set is now emptied and compiled again in full (firstrun.py). Workaround for an install that already failed: delete work\build-win (Linux folder: work/build) in the install folder and run run.cmd (run.sh) again.
  • FixedUltrawide and wide FOV: the sky's fog band (Level 6) is no longer cut off at the screen's sides with hard grey edges: the sky camera's near plane now comes closer for a view wider than the game's.
  • FixedUltrawide: the first-person weapon is no longer drawn half as large again as on a 16:9 screen (its FOV came from the camera's aspect, which the port widens).
  • FixedThe field of view setting widens the world: before, it reached only the sky's camera, so the world stayed at the game's FOV and the sky and far mountains slid against it when turning.
  • FixedThe pause menu's items no longer come back empty after opening one of its screens (Audio, Controls...) and going back: the PC item's list is made again with the game's own text format.
  • FixedVICTORY with the mouse: the statistics no longer darken under the pointer (the game keeps that list inactive), and Quit and Continue can be pointed at and clicked (also FAILED's Retry and Quit).
  • FixedButton prompts no longer turn back into PlayStation glyphs after a while (picking up and swapping weapons): the game reloads its button atlas over the same memory, and that copy now gets the player's glyphs again (patch 2060).
  • FixedUltrawide: Rico's grenade icons stay next to his M224-A3's ammo panel instead of near the middle of the screen.
  • FixedThe background of the VICTORY, FAILED and pause screens no longer turns into green static after a few levels in a long session: the game copies the frame into the screen's background texture when the screen opens, and with the MLAA on the GPU (the default) that copy was dropped, so the texture showed whatever a later level had left in that memory (patch 2059).
  • FixedThe main menu no longer stays black after quitting from the pause menu late in a long session: every movie leaked one of cellAudio's 8 notify slots, so the 8th movie of a session could not start its sound and never played, and the menu waited for it behind its fade (patch 3033).
  • FixedWidescreen: the picture no longer shrinks to 16:9 with bars and stretches back during gameplay. A frame that took over 200 ms (a hitch) counted as a 2D screen; now a 2D screen must also keep showing frames without a 3D picture.
  • FixedLong sessions no longer slow down to about 70 fps from the fifth or sixth level on: the PC menu's Lua script was compiled again at every script call in each new Lua state once 16 states had been seen (a level makes two to five). It is now given to each state once (8 levels in a row: 68 to 90 fps before, 140 to 145 after).
  • FixedBlack blocks over the menus and movies whenever the frame has bars (a 16:10 window or borderless display; AMD, issue #17): the window's present cleared the bars and copied the frame with no barrier between them, so the clear could land over the frame (patch 2053).
  • FixedWindows: a fullscreen window that loses the focus no longer goes headless ("the swapchain could not be recreated", issue #17): while minimized the window shows nothing, and the picture comes back when it is restored (patch 2054). Any other swapchain that cannot be recreated no longer closes the window either: the frames are skipped and the next presents try again, and the swapchain is also recreated after Alt+Enter, a restore or a move to another display at the same size (patch 2057, after Project Helghast and Project Pyrrhus on D3D12).
  • FixedWindows: PS3_GCM_MAX_QUEUED_FLIPS works. Its wait ended at once on Windows, so with V-Sync (FIFO, the only mode some AMD drivers offer) the menus and the opening movies ran 400 to 650 frames (3 to 4 s) ahead of the screen: slow menu input and stutter (issue #18). The Windows build under Wine now stays at 2 frames ahead (patch 2055). Between its checks the wait naps 100 us on a high-resolution timer, as on Linux, instead of Sleep(1) (at least 1 ms), which saw each flip up to a millisecond late (patch 2058, after sp00nznet/ps3recomp#628).
  • FixedWindows: LV2 145 (sys_time_get_current_time) returns the wall clock, not the time since the PC started (it read January 1970); the Linux build was right (patch 3032). The game's own dates come through cellRtc, which was already right, so no effect in play is known. Found by Project Pyrrhus (issue #27, after its patch 6057).
  • FixedAn update over an older install can no longer run the older build's translated shaders: the shader cache on disk (PS3RECOMP_VK_CACHE, default ~/.cache/ps3recomp-vk) was keyed by the program and a version number bumped by hand, so a build whose shader translator or glslang changed without the bump read the older SPIR-V as its own. Its files and pipeline list are now keyed by the translator's id, a hash of its sources and the glslang version; the first start after such an update builds the cache again (patch 2056). Not seen in this port; Project Pyrrhus lost its sight's reticle that way (its issue #25, fixed by its patch 6047).

5 Nov 2026 · pre-release

  • AddedTemporal upscalers on Linux and Windows (ENHANCEMENT, off by default): AMD FSR 3.1 and NVIDIA DLSS Super Resolution and DLAA, chosen on the PC page ("Temporal Upscaler (on restart)") or with PS3RECOMP_TEMPORAL, with the camera jittered and per-object motion vectors; the HUD is drawn at the output resolution (patches 2045 to 2052, docs/dev/upscalers.md). FSR 3.1 is in every build, from the FidelityFX SDK's files vendored in third_party/fidelityfx-fsr3/. DLSS is downloaded from NVIDIA on your machine only if you accept NVIDIA's DLSS SDK licence: when tools/install.sh or run.cmd asks (--dlss accept|decline), or with the Windows setup's "Download NVIDIA DLSS" box, unticked by default; no release carries NVIDIA's files.
  • AddedThe sprint motion blur runs on the GPU (patch 2043), also over an upscaled image (patch 2048).
  • AddedButton prompts: Kenney's Input Prompts (CC0) in the game's own finish, and pad pictures of our own for Xbox, Switch Pro and keyboard on the Controls screen, by the pad last touched (patch 4013).
  • AddedThe pipelines a run used are listed and built ahead on worker threads at the next start (patch 2044).
  • AddedDeveloper tools: Tracy zones (patch 3029), frame-time and per-thread CPU measurement (perf.cpp, tools/perf/), recorded input routes replayed with the sound on the route's clock (route.cpp, patch 3028), opt-in guest write tracking (patch 3031), and the motion blur harness (tools/mb_harness/).
  • AddedThe Windows setup program asks for your files on pages of its own (the game folder, the decrypted EBOOT, archive and libsre, and dev_flash for the music), checks their kind and size before copying anything, and builds the port in the wizard with a progress bar and a Stop button; when the build stops it says why and opens the log. Silent installs take the files as switches (/GAME= and the others). After Project Helghast's and Project Pyrrhus's setup programs (MIT). release.yml installs it on the Windows runner with stand-ins for the files (tools/release/fake_game_files.py) and checks that the build runs and stops at the check.
  • AddedStart menu entries "Verify and rebuild" (checks the installed files, then your game files, and rebuilds what changed), "Open saves folder" and "Make a support package" (a zip of the logs and settings for a bug report, without your user name, saves or game files). After Project Helghast's (MIT).
  • AddedThe setup refuses install folders the build cannot use ([ ] ; in the path, OneDrive, system and profile folders), also for silent installs. Installing over an earlier version replaces the payload's folders whole, so nothing stale is left, and keeps the build, the game folder and the saves. The uninstaller asks whether to delete the saves and settings (default No).
  • AddedThe setup program is dark, with side and header images for every screen scale and its own setup and uninstall icons (tools/release/installer_art.py).
  • AddedThe Linux release folder (tools/release/assemble_payload.py --platform linux --tar): the port's sources, the patched ps3recomp and a pinned toolchain (Zig 0.17.0 as the C and C++ compiler, CMake, Ninja, SDL2, zlib, glslang, the Vulkan headers and FFmpeg 9's libraries), so a player needs only the usual desktop libraries (Python 3.10 or newer, glibc 2.31 or newer, SDL2, a Vulkan driver). run.sh asks for your files and builds there, play.sh starts the game. The binaries target glibc 2.31 (port/cmake/zig-linux.cmake, tools/release/zig/, tools/release/build_linux_deps.py); KZ_LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=pinned selects that toolchain in a source checkout too.
  • AddedReleases after 0.2.0 carry that folder as project-vekta-X.Y.Z-linux.tar.gz: .github/workflows/release.yml builds it and checks it in a Debian 11 container with no compiler (tools/release/check_linux_folder.sh).
  • ChangedThe lifted PPU functions take their context as __restrict (patch 3030).
  • ChangedA copy the setup program installed keeps its saves and settings in %APPDATA%\Project Vekta, so a new install or an uninstall leaves them alone; the setup's "Portable" option keeps them in the install folder instead. Saves an earlier version left in the install folder move there on the next start.
  • FixedWindows: the launcher stopped the game the moment it started whenever the last session's log (work\play.log) ended with its window being closed: it read that old log before the new game had emptied it. An install over an earlier version kept that log, so the game never opened until the old version was uninstalled; any start after a session closed by its window could hit it too. The launcher now empties the log before it starts the game.
  • FixedInstalling over an earlier version: on a tester's Windows machine the game started and closed again at once, with nothing on screen, until the old version was uninstalled (its log went with the uninstall). The lift now starts from empty output folders, so no source an earlier version lifted is compiled in; the build now configures CMake afresh when the build folder was made from another version or patch set (firstrun.py); the launcher rebuilds before playing when the build there is not the one the installed files make (another version, patch set or DLSS choice, as when the setup's build was skipped or stopped); and a game that stops within 20 seconds of starting gets a message with the end of its log instead of silence.
  • FixedThe Linux folder's build no longer stops at the compile step with "unknown CPU: 'x86'": its Zig wrappers spell the port's -march=x86-64-v3 the way Zig names CPUs (x86_64_v3).
  • FixedThe Linux folder's link no longer fails on mallinfo2 (glibc 2.33; the folder targets 2.31): the stats line's heap count looks it up at run time and falls back to mallinfo.
  • FixedThe limit of flips the game may queue ahead of the screen (PS3_GCM_MAX_QUEUED_FLIPS, default 2) no longer drifts: each flip done at once, instead of queued in the command buffer, loosened it by one for good (patch 2040). The queued value in the [kz-stats] lines stays at the real count.
  • FixedWindows: a controller that was detected but gave no input (seen on a OneXPlayer X2 Mini Pro's built-in Xbox-style pad, issue #19) works without setting SDL_JOYSTICK_RAWINPUT=0 by hand: the port turns SDL's Raw Input joystick driver off (patch 4012). Setting SDL_JOYSTICK_RAWINPUT=1 brings it back.
  • FixedGitHub shows the licence as MIT again (it read "Other", issue #27): LICENSE holds the MIT text alone, and the note that it covers only the port, not the game, moved to NOTICE.md and the README. Same terms as before.

The whole changelog >

About the port

how it works · ps3recomp v0.19.0 · 139 patches

The port is built on ps3recomp (MIT), pinned at v0.19.0 with 139 patches of this project: the PPU code and the game's SPU programs are lifted to C++, the PS3 system libraries the game calls are reimplemented, and the game's RSX command stream is replayed on Vulkan. It builds natively on Linux, and on Linux for Windows; the Windows build is tested under Wine, Proton and on Windows.

It follows Project Helghast and Project Pyrrhus, the same method applied to Killzone 3 and Killzone 2, and reuses their general runtime work. About 65 % of Killzone HD is done, and 43 % of the whole trilogy plan; what comes next: the roadmap.

Full status

Install

v0.4.0 pre-release

9 Nov 2026 · partly playable · source for Linux x64

Download v0.4.0All releases

The release page has project-vekta-0.4.0-source.tar.gz (this version's tree with ps3recomp at its pinned commit) with a .sha256 file, and SHA256SUMS: check your download against them. There is no installer yet: the archive builds the port as below.

The build checks your own Killzone HD files, translates the game's code and builds it on your machine. Nothing of the game is shipped or downloaded, and nothing is written into your game files. What each input must contain: Getting your files.

git clone --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/gustavomorinaga/project-vekta
cd project-vekta
tools/check-game-files.py
tools/ps3recomp-patched.sh
tools/lift.sh
tools/setup-vfs.sh
tools/build.sh
tools/play.sh

The steps, and the Windows build: building.

What goes online

Nothing. The port, its scripts and the build make no network connection of their own; the only downloads are the ones you start (this repository, its ps3recomp submodule, your system's packages). Where your saves and settings go: the README.

Viewing this website loads the Fira Sans Condensed font from Google Fonts, which sees your visit; the repository, the build and the game do not.

Requirements

What you need

Your own Killzone HD (NPUA80856) from the Killzone Trilogy disc, installed, with its decrypted EBOOT and data archive, and the decrypted libsre and dev_flash of PS3 system software 4.93: GETTING-FILES.md. No PlayStation Network account is used.

Operating systemLinux x64; Windows x64 (other Windows versions and machines not tried)CachyOS (Linux x64); the maintainer's Windows install for the cross-built exe; Wine and Proton (GE-Proton 11, proton-cachyos)
CPUx86-64 with AVX2 (x86-64-v3, Intel Haswell or AMD Zen and newer), the default build target; KZ_MARCH="" builds for any x86-64, untestedthe maintainer's desktop CPU with AVX-512 (KZ_MARCH=x86-64-v4)
GPUa Vulkan GPU and driver; NVIDIA DLSS needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU, AMD FSR 3.1 runs on any; a tester's AMD Radeon 8060S on Windows runs it with open problems (KNOWN_ISSUES.md, issues #17 and #18), other GPUs not tried yetNVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti, driver 615
Memorybuilding: several GB for the lifted code (use fewer jobs on small machines); playing: not measured
Diskabout 4 GB for the game files, plus the build (work/), a few GB

Details: requirements.md. The tested column is the maintainer's machine; reports from other hardware are welcome.

About

Notice and creditsLicence (MIT)Project HelghastProject Pyrrhus

Killzone and Killzone HD are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla Games; the names are used only to say which game the port runs. "Vekta" is the name of the game's own colony world. No game content is distributed: no disc or PSN files, no decrypted or translated game code, no assets, no firmware and no keys. Players supply their own copy of the game; the game's code is translated and compiled on the player's own machine from their own files.

The port's own code, tools and documentation are MIT. Third-party components and credits: NOTICE.md. Temporal upscaling: AMD FidelityFX FSR 3.1 (MIT, built in) and NVIDIA DLSS (NVIDIA's, under its own licence; downloaded from NVIDIA on the player's machine only when they accept it, and never distributed here). AMD, FidelityFX, NVIDIA and DLSS are trademarks of their owners.
